title: Draft: GitLab CI+CMake: Start migrating away from vcvars*.bat.
description:
Start building our Windows jobs using a vanilla environment instead of
one configured using one of the vcvars*.bat scripts.

Note that we use MSVC_REDIST_DIR from CMake's
InstallRequiredSystemLibraries, which might not be the wisest course
of action.

Partial fix for #17534.

notes.body: Marking as a draft since this shouldn't be committed in its current form.

Note that if you want to keep the check, I find that the `PLATFORM` environment variable is set to x86 in the 32-bit variant.  So instead of checking against `[undefined]` perhaps you could check against `x86`.

If you feel like this is potentially dangerous and stupid, here is a possible alternative:

Starting basis:  `CMAKE_GENERATOR_INSTANCE` matches the `VSINSTALLDIR` transient variable used by vcvars to calculate `VCINSTALLDIR` (The latter being the former with `VC` tacked onto the end).  If the environment variable is not defined, it seems like a fine substitute.  

Starting in VS 2019 it appears MS has introduced the merge modules and the redistributable installers into a sanely named folder called v142 (aka v + the CRT version) in addition to the more cryptic MS version.  That should vastly simplify looking it up because it is simply `${VCINSTALLDIR}/Redist/MSVC/v${MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION}/` (Note: `MSVC_TOOLSET_VERSION` is provided by CMake and is 141 in 2017 and 142 in 2019 as expected so it doesn't need to be calculated as it is in the WIX project).  

For 2017 and earlier, the trick that NSIS uses should suffice as well:

```
file(GLOB _ms_vcredist_subdir RELATIVE "${VCINSTALLDIR}"
		"${VCINSTALLDIR}/Redist/MSVC/14.*.*")
```

This should eliminate any dependency on the CMake module.  Hope this is helpful if only as food for thought!
